lxc_7aa49e59bbd91af2.text: Horse riding means sitting on a horse and moving with it.

lxc_cb7ba159a4cb20ad.text: A good rider learns slowly, wears safe clothes, and is kind to the horse.

lxc_9ee453df54854cbe.text: People ride horses for fun, work, and sport.

lxc_bacc6eb65cfe04d1.text: Some people enjoy a quiet ride outside.

lxc_5c99346a802825ff.text: Police officers may ride horses at work.

lxc_b0ff44eefa8115f8.text: In the Olympic Games, riders do sports such as jumping and dressage.

lxc_c1e6de13f8ea1d7a.text: In dressage, the horse does careful moves when the rider asks.

lxc_e163e57abad2a47f.text: Horse riding is teamwork: the rider gives small signs, and the horse answers.

lxc_15fb31103620250f.text: Horse riding for kids starts slowly at a riding school.

lxc_a73a21489490327d.text: Charlotte Dujardin also began with a quiet walk, not a race.

lxc_29a3d146a12befb3.text: A new rider should start at a good riding school with a teacher.

lxc_06e8fb38c5fca218.text: The first horse is often quiet and kind.

lxc_69c873c009168ea7.text: The teacher may lead the horse around an arena, which is a safe place for riding.

lxc_bfe47cfd332729a6.text: Sometimes the rider tries a short trot, which feels more bouncy.

lxc_7acf61aea495456c.text: There is no need to hurry.

lxc_0b138c9f74efd03e.text: Always wear a riding helmet that fits well and is closed under your chin.

lxc_f1ddade2062e122e.text: A riding helmet helps protect your head if you fall.

lxc_b46778aee78ebf8c.text: Wear strong boots that cover your ankles.

lxc_c2a5be875f824f85.text: Do not walk behind a horse because it may kick.

lxc_56ffef06dd4ea9ec.text: Walk to the horse from the side.

lxc_83ca658ab094bd36.text: Talk softly and move gently, so the horse knows you are there.

lxc_39fda23bad58ca99.text: A saddle is the seat on the horse’s back.

lxc_b5a894ee2e0c7509.text: A strap under the horse holds it in place.

lxc_7223fcbbf7ddd923.text: The saddle spreads the rider’s weight across the horse’s back.

lxc_f2cb6cc86dd93524.text: This helps the horse stay comfortable.

lxc_daead9bec066c360.text: Stirrups hang on both sides of the saddle.

lxc_4e53467a6160f4fe.text: The rider puts a foot in each stirrup for balance.

lxc_1ba4f721e23ff8c8.text: Boots with heels help stop the feet from sliding through.

lxc_a4471b353e0c74c7.text: Reins are long straps that go from the rider’s hands to the horse’s bridle.

lxc_6cec57d552af6d05.text: The bridle is the gear on the horse’s head.

lxc_3f86c3cd3b33d52b.text: Reins help a rider ask the horse to turn, slow down, or stop.

lxc_2ded5fc31b2ceffa.text: They are a little like a steering wheel, but riders must use small, soft moves.

lxc_09bd5aaa4d99a6ab.text: Pulling hard can hurt the horse.

lxc_4963bf2b26933fbe.text: Riders also use their legs and body.

lxc_e5183231849b8bbf.text: Charlotte Dujardin rode Valegro in dressage.

lxc_69d912a8dbb37510.text: They won individual Olympic gold in London in 2012 and Rio in 2016.

lxc_58e16c2df67fea27.text: Frankie Dettori was a famous race rider.

lxc_b4f86c314065f2c8.text: In 1996, he won all seven races on one day at Ascot.

lxc_317dd5d852685f62.text: Ron Turcotte rode the fast racehorse Secretariat, which won the US Triple Crown in 1973.
